FD1.quote: Every lookup raises `Faraday::Error: :retry is not registered on Faraday::Request` (provider.rb:37). ... `CitationEnrichmentJob`'s `retry_on` ... never fires. Every enrichment fails outright ... Add `gem "faraday-retry", "~> 2.2"` to the Gemfile. Bundler auto-requires `faraday/retry`. ... The first test (503 then 200) must record 2 requests ... persistent-503 test must record exactly 6 requests ... a single 401 makes exactly 1 request
FD1.reasons: Impact: the plan says enrichments fail outright and land in Failed, but the key says citations stay pending and fall into Sidekiq retries. Validation: test-suite counts only, with no real HTTP provider or Sidekiq worker, no check for empty scheduled/retry/dead sets, no check of zero requests and pending citations on the unrepaired target, and no isolation of FD1 with FD2 repaired.

FD2.quote: On 2.12.2 it raises `Faraday::Error: :basic_auth is not registered on Faraday::Request`, which is uncaught, same as R2. ... Change line 38 to `faraday.request :authorization, :basic, @user, @password`. ... byte-identical to what `:basic_auth` sends on 1.10.4.
FD2.reasons: Impact: 'same as R2' inherits the wrong 'fails outright' consequence instead of pending citations with fallback retries. Validation: test-adapter header probe and suite assertions only, with no real HTTP check after FD1 is repaired, no fresh-process numeric/colon/hash credentials, no real wrong-password 401, and no refresh, ownership or unsafe-metadata controls.
